study_purpose.text: This study aims to investigate whether the duration of the 5R-STS test predicts the outcome of low back operations after one year.

who_may_join.text: Anyone affected by sciatica may join this study.

procedures_or_participation.text: Participants will undergo a 5R-STS test where they stand up and sit down five times from a chair without armrests, counting the number of movements. They will also complete an interview about their age, education level, smoking history, mood, quality of life, and stress.

risks_or_burdens.text: There are no risks or burdens mentioned in the provided evidence.

time_commitment.text: The procedures involve a 1-hour interview and a 2-5 minute 5R-STS test.

what_is_unclear: Not clearly stated in the retrieved evidence

patient_facing_summary.text: This study investigates if a test measuring how often someone can stand up and sit down from a chair can predict the success of back surgery. Anyone with sciatica can join. They will be interviewed and asked to do a 5R-STS test.
